results: At every actual unit Fourier frequency the derivative of an absolutely continuous function includes its EXACT endpoint jump. L2 data and an L1 forcing satisfying a Fourier derivative equation with a constant defect recover an absolutely continuous representative on the ENTIRE closed interval; its endpoint jump is minus the defect. Periodicity of the representative or derivative is not assumed.

The physical product of ANY two interval L2 functions has actual Fourier coefficients given by the FULL unconditionally convergent convolution of their unit coefficients. There is no extra Wiener or H1 hypothesis on either factor.

An interval L2 weak solution of v'=u*v+b, with arbitrary L2 coefficient and L2 forcing and an arbitrary constant boundary defect, has a full interval H1 representative. The recovered function has the prescribed almost-everywhere first-order ODE and EXACT endpoint jump. Its continuous representative makes u*v L2 and yields actual L2 derivative regularity.

The native H1 inclusion, unit-period derivative and multiplication by every L2 potential are identified with their literal physical unit-interval L2 functions. Their normalization is the original multiplier 2*pi*i*n; physical and Fourier representatives agree almost everywhere without smoothness assumptions.

For a native Dirichlet Miura eigenvector, the original coefficient quasi-derivative starts in L2. Exact period doubling transports the full distributional factorization. The resulting first-order coefficient equation contains the CENTRAL native residual as its boundary defect; that defect is not set to zero.

The native Miura weak eigen-equation recovers a full interval H1 quasi-derivative G. The pair consisting of the original H1 position and G satisfies BOTH literal physical quasi-Hill rows almost everywhere, and G(1)-G(0) is exactly the native central residual. No extra endpoint condition is imposed on G.

The recovered native Miura pair is an ACTUAL independently defined absolutely continuous Dirichlet weak state agreeing with the native position at EVERY closed-interval point. A nonzero native vector gives a nonzero scalar state and forces the independently normalized rough Dirichlet characteristic to vanish.

For EVERY complex original unit-period H-minus-one potential and EVERY complex energy, each nonzero native H1-to-H-minus-one Dirichlet eigenvector forces the entire normalized characteristic to vanish. The actual shifted Miura chart is selected by the proof, and the exact native constant-shift identity removes the shift. No realness, nonzero energy, high-frequency cutoff or supplied lift is assumed. The theorem also covers actual base-space eigenvectors of the Dirichlet partial operator.

On the article ENTIRE original real mean-zero physically period-one H-minus-one distribution domain, the same necessary characteristic condition is proved for the actual native weak and partial operators. Every native eigenvalue belongs to the complete original ordered characteristic-label sequence, including ALL central indices. The original distribution is retained unchanged on every smooth test.
essential_remaining: Prove the CONVERSE: an independent AC quasi-derivative Dirichlet state, or a normalized characteristic zero, yields a nonzero native H1-to-H-minus-one eigenvector for EVERY complex original H-minus-one source potential. Native-eigenvector-to-state and native-eigenvalue-to-characteristic-zero are now proved without extra regularity or boundary assumptions.

Prove native Dirichlet partial-operator closedness and resolvent properties; identify its ENTIRE spectrum and ALGEBRAIC multiplicities with the normalized characteristic. Necessity for actual nonzero native eigenvectors does not establish characteristic-zero sufficiency, absence of other spectrum, compact resolvent or algebraic multiplicity agreement.

Complete global COMPLEX Dirichlet central labels and the full COMPLEX general-weight midpoint estimate/local boundedness in source Theorem 2.1(ii). Full REAL characteristic labels, analytic multiplicities, original n-times-L2 asymptotic, free values and weighted midpoint membership remain proved; no uniform real norm-ball midpoint estimate is inferred.

Complete remaining low periodic simplicity/interlacing and periodic/antiperiodic boundary parity, general complex-ratio Lemma 2.20, original KdV Birkhoff maps and actual H-minus-one approximation flow. Main Theorems 1.1,1.3,1.4,5.1,5.9 remain UNPROVED.
